newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill market sidelined by Thai float.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill market sidelined by Thai float.

text.p: Manila banks stayed away from the secondary T-bill market after the Central Bank two successive increases in its key rate, traders said.
The Central Bank was forced to defend the peso after Thailand announced it would allow a managed float of its currency.
"No one wants to move at this point in time until the market settles down," a dealer said.
Traders said buying in the market was limited to servicing clients' requirements.
A Reuters poll of six financial institutions gave higher bid and offer rates after the Central Bank decided to offer one-day reverse repos at 20 percent and later at 24 percent.
The average interbank call loan rate rose slightly to 15.09375 percent from 15.0625 percent after some cash was sucked by the Central Bank's dollar sales.
Volume was lower at billion pesos from 28.68 billion pesos. The market had 32 lenders and 24 borrowers.
